sections.heading: Glossary term: Cosmological Principle
sections.body: The cosmological principle is the basis for modern cosmology and is built on observations and a fundamental assumption. It states that spatially the Universe is isotropic and homogeneous on large scales (scales larger than a few hundred million light years). Observations on sufficiently large scales, show that the Universe appears to "look" the same in any direction; there is no preferred direction (isotropic). The fundamental assumption, based on the Copernican Principle (humans do not occupy a special location in the Universe), is that the Universe is the same everywhere (homogeneous); there appears to be no preferred location. The cosmological principle is accompanied by universality, where the laws of physics and the fundamental constants are the same everywhere in the Universe: here on Earth or in a distant galaxy.

Glossary term: Cosmological Principle

Description: The cosmological principle is the basis for modern cosmology and is built on observations and a fundamental assumption. It states that spatially the Universe is isotropic and homogeneous on large scales (scales larger than a few hundred million light years). Observations on sufficiently large scales, show that the Universe appears to "look" the same in any direction; there is no preferred direction (isotropic). The fundamental assumption, based on the Copernican Principle (humans do not occupy a special location in the Universe), is that the Universe is the same everywhere (homogeneous); there appears to be no preferred location. The cosmological principle is accompanied by universality, where the laws of physics and the fundamental constants are the same everywhere in the Universe: here on Earth or in a distant galaxy.

Related Terms:

  • Cosmology
  • Copernican Principle


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. sections.body_ru: Космологический принцип является основой современной космологии и опирается на наблюдения и фундаментальное предположение. Он утверждает, что в пространстве Вселенная изотропна и однородна на больших масштабах (масштабах, превышающих несколько сотен миллионов световых лет). Наблюдения на достаточно больших масштабах показывают, что Вселенная выглядит одинаково в любом направлении; нет предпочтительного направления (изотропность). Фундаментальное предположение, основанное на принципе Коперника (люди не занимают особого положения во Вселенной), состоит в том, что Вселенная везде одинакова (однородность); по-видимому, нет предпочтительного местоположения. Космологический принцип сопровождается универсальностью, согласно которой законы физики и фундаментальные постоянные одинаковы везде во Вселенной: здесь на Земле или в далёкой галактике.
